historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2027 revenue guidance midpoint (+9.1%, 2026-08-25 8-K) rounded up for Intuit's habit of guiding conservatively at the start of the year; the equity CAGR is rejected as the anchor because buybacks ($5.4B) and dividends ($1.3B) exceed retained earnings and compress book value (see divergence warning).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 3.2% diverges >30% from revenue (14.3%) and EPS (24.9%): capital returns of $6.8B in FY26 alone shrink book value, so equity growth says nothing about the business's growth. The 5yr equity CAGR (14.0%) is inflated by the FY22 Mailchimp stock issuance.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award withholding taxes; interest income not stripped because Intuit has been net-debt since FY2020). Owner FCF CAGRs exceed reported-FCF CAGRs only because FY26 owner FCF is flattered by ~$1.1B of OBBBA cash-tax deferral; on a tax-normalised FY26 owner FCF of ~$4,830m the 3yr/5yr CAGRs are 24.7%/18.6%, closer to reported. Within the window SBC + withholding grew faster than cash flow FY21-FY24 (owner FCF fell to $1,751m in FY24 while reported FCF rose), then reversed in FY25-26 as SBC fell from 11.9% to 9.6% of revenue and withholding cash dropped with the share price.

scenario_narratives.base: Intuit compounds revenue at high single digits: Global Business Solutions (QuickBooks Online, payments, payroll, the mid-market Enterprise Suite cohort growing ~38%) carries the growth at 13-14%, Consumer grows low-to-mid single digits with Credit Karma (+11-13%) offsetting a mature TurboTax (+2-3%), and Mailchimp is flat. The 2026 restructuring (~3,000 roles) lifts GAAP operating margin ~4pp in FY27 per guidance and pre-SBC EBITDA ramps from 44% to 46% over five years. SBC plus withholding glides from 11.2% to 8.5% of revenue, acquired-intangible amortisation rolls off, and cash tax normalises to 24% after the FY26-27 OBBBA deferral. Owner FCF grows from ~$6.3B in FY27 toward ~$11B by FY36. Value is derived from the guided FY27 cost base and the component build; the current price implies the bear path.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI-native product strategy works in Intuit's favour rather than against it: Intuit Assist and agentic bookkeeping raise QuickBooks ARPU and attach rates, Enterprise Suite opens the $89B mid-market, TurboTax Live/Full Service keep taking share from assisted filers, and Credit Karma's cross-sell with TurboTax lifts blended monetisation. Revenue compounds at ~11% for three years, decelerating to 4.5% by year 10, and margins reach 48% as AI lowers service and support cost. SBC falls to 7.5% of revenue.
scenario_narratives.bear: The market's current thesis plays out: AI assistants and free tools commoditise DIY tax filing and simple SMB accounting, a revived government free-file option caps TurboTax pricing, Mailchimp declines, and Credit Karma turns down with a consumer-credit cycle. Growth fades to ~1.5% after FY29, pre-SBC EBITDA compresses to 38%, and a depressed share price keeps SBC above 10% of revenue as grants are sized to hold dollar comp. FTC 'free' order and privacy/AI regulation add cost. Terminal value is capped at 15x on 2% growth.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF with SBC and equity-award withholding fully expensed and the share count held flat; the FY26 cash-tax windfall (~$1.1B, OBBBA R&D expensing catch-up) is normalised away rather than capitalised; margins are built from guided FY27 GAAP operating income plus D&A and SBC, then ramped modestly; acquired-intangible amortisation is allowed to roll off. Three scenarios are weighted 25/50/25 with a single 9.5% WACC. The house (SBC-expensed) value is the headline; the street (SBC as non-cash) value is reported as the upper bound of the accounting-regime band.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI agents / free tools commoditising DIY tax prep and simple SMB bookkeeping -- the single axis that separates bear from base and the one the market is currently pricing
Revival of an IRS Direct File or state free-file programme capping TurboTax pricing and low-end share
Credit Karma revenue (~13% of total) is tied to lender/insurer marketing budgets and consumer credit conditions
Restructuring execution: a 17% workforce cut during an AI product transition can hit product delivery and support quality
SBC + withholding is the largest single deduction (~$2.8B FY26, 12.9% of revenue); if a depressed share price forces larger grants the glide to 8.5% does not happen

Cash tax normalisation: the model assumes the OBBBA benefit is largely spent by FY28; if it persists longer the near-term flows are understated, if the FY27 residual is smaller than 17% they are overstated
Terminal value is ~60% of EV at a 9.5% WACC; each 1pp of WACC moves base value roughly 15-20%

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API regular close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 252.84-703.96.
data_sources.financials: research/INTU/Reports/INTU_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL-derived, FY2008-FY2026, July fiscal year) for revenue, operating income, net income, EPS, OCF, capex, SBC, equity, cash, shares; SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 896878) FY2024-FY2026 for depreciation, acquired-intangible amortisation, income tax expense and cash taxes paid, deferred tax, tax-withholding payments, buybacks, dividends, LongTermDebt split, operating lease liabilities, shares outstanding; Q4 FY2026 earnings press release (8-K exhibit, 2026-08-25) for FY2027 guidance, total debt ($7.7B) and cash-and-investments ($7.2B).
data_sources.qualitative: research/INTU/Reports/INTU_Analysis.json (2026-09-29) for business model, segment mix, moat, risks and bull/bear points; its EPS guidance items were cross-checked against the 8-K (non-GAAP now includes SBC from FY27).

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 2026-07-31: 268.384m basic shares outstanding (10-K balance sheet) plus ~1.0m dilutive RSUs/options (FY26 weighted diluted 277m less basic 276m). Cover page shows 267.236m basic at 2026-08-31, so the count is still falling. Held FLAT because SBC (incl. withholding taxes) is fully expensed in the flows; charging dilution too would double-count. The FY26 weighted-average diluted 277m in the CSV overstates the current count after $5.4B of buybacks.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement: ShareBasedCompensation add-back $2,056m plus PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation $709m (financing activities), summed because Intuit publishes no combined SBC-plus-withholding figure. Both from SEC XBRL companyfacts, CIK 896878.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD WACC. Cost of equity ~9.9% (10y UST ~4.2%, ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.15 for a large-cap US software/fintech platform). Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.8% (2026 senior notes), ~3.7% after tax. Market-value weights ~91% equity / 9% debt ($72.6B market cap vs $7.7B debt) give ~9.4%; rounded to 9.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios -- risk is charged in the scenario paths and weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A): operating lease cost ($124m FY26 payments) sits inside GAAP operating income and therefore inside the EBITDA margin path; operating lease liabilities ($752m) are NOT added to net debt. Immaterial at <0.6% of revenue.
inputs.nci_treatment: None -- Intuit has no non-controlling interests.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Total debt $7,669m = LongTermDebt XBRL tag at 2026-07-31 ($1,249m current + $6,420m non-current), confirmed by the Q4 FY26 press release ('total debt was $7.7 billion'). The Metrics.csv TotalDebt of $8,918m double-counts the current portion (same pattern in FY2024: 6,537 = 6,038 + 499) and is not used. Cash of $7,200m is 'cash and investments' per the same press release (cash and equivalents $4,705m plus ~$2.5B of investments). Funds receivable and amounts held for customers (payroll/payments float) are excluded on both sides. Net debt is positive, so interest income is left in the flows (nothing to strip; the unlevered build ignores both interest income and the ~$295m interest paid).
inputs.cash_tax_note: FY26 cash taxes paid were $281m against a $1,451m GAAP provision (deferred tax expense +$1,279m): the OBBBA restoration of immediate domestic R&D expensing plus the catch-up deduction of previously capitalised R&D. Reported FY26 FCF is flattered by ~$1.1B that does not recur. Cash tax rate ramps 17% (FY27, residual catch-up) -> 22% -> 24% steady state, matching the ~24% GAAP effective rate now that excess stock-comp tax benefits have shrunk with the share price.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component-built, 10-year explicit horizon (SBC%, D&A% and cash-tax paths are all still ramping at year 5), scenario-weighted -- SKILL.md routing row 'Operating company: tech, SaaS, consumer internet'. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY entry). FY0 is FY2026 (year ended 2026-07-31). Anchor for FY27 is the 2026-08-25 guidance: revenue +9-10%, GAAP operating income $7,408-7,490m (+26-27%, restructuring savings landing), and from FY27 Intuit's own non-GAAP includes SBC. FY0 component check: GAAP operating income $5,884m + D&A $672m (depreciation $187m + acquired-intangible amortisation $485m) + SBC $2,056m = pre-SBC EBITDA $8,612m = 40.2% of revenue (41.5% excluding the $293m FY26 restructuring charge). FY27 base path implies GAAP EBIT (EBITDA - SBC expense - D&A) of ~$7.5B, inside the guided range. D&A runs well above capex because Credit Karma/Mailchimp intangible amortisation (~$485m) is non-cash and rolling off; da_pct_path declines toward capex. Capex includes capitalised software ($46m). Buyback of $5,412m in FY26 (plus $1,347m dividends) means the flat share count IS being funded in cash -- a repurchaser. The share price sits 62% below its 52-week high; the market is pricing something close to the bear path (AI agents commoditising DIY tax and SMB bookkeeping). The model is anchored to guidance and the component build, not to the price.
inputs.price_note: Yahoo Finance chart API regular close on 2026-09-28 (not after-hours); 52-week range 252.84-703.96. The stock has fallen ~62% from its high; the print is a regular close and not flagged volatile.

bear.rationale: FY27 lands at the bottom of the guide, then AI agents and free/low-cost tools commoditise DIY tax and simple SMB bookkeeping: TurboTax units and price erode, QuickBooks net adds stall, Credit Karma turns down with the credit cycle, Mailchimp shrinks. Pricing pressure plus AI compute compress pre-SBC EBITDA to 38%; SBC stays above 10% because a low share price forces larger grants to hold comp. Terminal growth 2%, 15x cap for an ex-growth franchise.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 at the top of the +9-10% guide (GBS +13-14%, Consumer +4-6%, Mailchimp flat), decelerating ~0.5pp/yr as QuickBooks mid-market/Enterprise Suite and Credit Karma offset a low-single-digit TurboTax and a flat Mailchimp; 4.5% by year 10 ahead of 3% terminal.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC EBITDA 44.0% in FY27 = guided GAAP operating income midpoint $7,449m + D&A ~$680m + SBC expense ~$2,160m (9.2% of revenue), on $23.4B revenue. FY26 was 40.2% (41.5% ex restructuring); the 17% workforce reduction is what lifts FY27. Ramps 0.5pp/yr to 46% as AI-assisted support and bookkeeping lower service cost, then flat -- AI compute and TurboTax marketing cap further expansion.
base.sbc_rationale: Combined SBC + withholding: 12.9% of revenue in FY26 (9.6% expense + 3.3% withholding). FY27 11.2% -- SBC expense ~9.2% (continuing the 11.9% -> 10.5% -> 9.6% FY24-26 trend) plus ~2% withholding, lower because awards now vest at a share price ~60% below grant. Glides 0.3pp/yr to 8.5%.
base.da_capex_rationale: D&A 3.1% in FY26 of which 2.3pp is acquired-intangible amortisation rolling off (Credit Karma Dec-20, Mailchimp Nov-21 deals); path declines to 1.4% (depreciation ~0.9% + residual). Capex (PP&E + capitalised software) 1.0% FY26, 1.5% FY24; 1.1% held.
base.tax_rationale: See inputs.cash_tax_note: 17% FY27 (residual OBBBA catch-up), 22% FY28, 24% thereafter (FY26 GAAP effective rate 24.1%).
base.wc_rationale: Deferred revenue rose $51m on a $2,617m revenue increase in FY26 (2%), $142m on $2,546m in FY25 (5.6%), fell $49m in FY24. 2% capture; TurboTax is transactional and QuickBooks is monthly-billed, so the prepaid tailwind is small.

bull.rationale: Beats the guide by ~1.5pp as in most pre-FY26 years: Enterprise Suite/QBO Advanced keep compounding at 30%+, Credit Karma holds low-teens, TurboTax Live/Full Service mix lifts ARPU, Mailchimp stabilises as a standalone segment. Restructuring savings plus AI-assisted service drive margins to 48%; SBC glides to 7.5% as headcount stays lean.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25%: the AI-commoditisation thesis is a live structural question for DIY tax and SMB bookkeeping, not idle pessimism -- it is what a 62% drawdown is pricing -- and the Direct File / FTC overhang recurs politically; there is no solvency or covenant risk (net debt ~$0.5B against ~$6B of owner FCF), which is why it is not higher. Bull cut to 25%: it needs mid-market Enterprise Suite, AI ARPU uplift and Credit Karma's credit cycle to all go right at once.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
